objective: Correct anonymous policy acknowledgement and stale-session restoration without affecting BUKLOD core features.
productionBaselineEvidence: verified: inspected main commit 6cc7ac0f594c1a852c8b8b27bf2d70c018a73bf8; Supabase production at 2026-10-31 09:17 PH reported accept_required_policy HTTP 400 and auth.uid() null, bearer was publishable key. No verified device OTA adoption or exact current runtime fingerprint; this manifest does not authorize release.
chosenApproach: Gate persisted-session fallback to explicit offline state; recover through Supabase SDK when connectivity returns; verify current SDK user and server policy state before persisting acceptance; hold boot spinner during reconnection instead of redirecting.
selectionRationale: Source evidence identifies shadow identity and unchecked acknowledgement caching; use existing auth SDK and policy RPC without schema/permission changes, cross-app rewrites or retry storms.
alternativeApproaches: Make policy RPC accept anonymous users (rejected: breaks identity and policy audit security).
Always clear cached sessions and force password login on every network drop (rejected: destroys offline access and harms weak-network reliability).
preserveBehaviors: Community Wall, Connect, Cluster, Show Faith and Quiz remain unmodified.
Offline accepted policy state may release read-only shell; offline cannot save acknowledgement.
Do not change server RLS, profile permission model, API keys or release runtime.
No automatic mutation retry, no authentication bypass or cross-account acceptance.
Keep new acknowledgement gated by server read-back.
acceptanceChecks: Missing SDK session never calls accept_required_policy.
Anonymous project-key request no longer gets a cached logged-in online shell.
Correct SDK user and server accepted policy rows are required before success.
Network outage and session expiry produce actionable feedback without accepting locally.
Boot spinner guards prevent transient login redirect on offline-to-online restoration.
Run focused pure Node contract and source guard tests, TypeScript compile and scoped engineering checks before RC.
Do not publish Android OTA without verified exact RC runtime and artifact.
